subject: Batch decline pattern + split-invoice recovery plan for Collectify
messages:
From: Eli Navarro <eli@collectify.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: billing@collectify.com
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Multiple card declines today — urgent help?

Hi Logan,

We saw a large spike of failed card authorizations for multiple customers on our weekly payout run this morning. 12 transactions from high-value customers failed with the same decline code from the acquirer. Our finance team is asking for:

- A breakdown of which invoices were affected (invoice IDs + amounts)
- Any evidence we can pass to our acquiring bank that these were legitimate charges (AVS, mask, response codes)
- A recovery path: do you support splitting an invoice so we can attempt a different card per invoice or retry logic tied to 3DS fallback?

I've attached a CSV with the raw decline lines. Can someone from Redwood confirm whether this looks like an acquirer-side routing issue versus tokenization/auth problem on your end? This is blocking our accounting close.

Thanks,
Eli Navarro
Head of Finance
Collectify, Inc.

Attachments: collectify_batch-decline-log-0609.csv
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Eli Navarro <eli@collectify.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 09:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Multiple card declines today — urgent help?

Eli — thanks for the quick report and the CSV. I pulled the decline rows and started a preliminary triage. Quick summary:

- Decline code cluster: PROCESSOR_DECLINE_54 (soft decline for insufficient funds / auth hold in many acquirers) but the acquirer responses include a routing hint that several authorizations were redirected to a 3rd-party gateway and then timed out.
- Tokenization: looks intact for the affected tokens (no mismatched fingerprints).
- Pattern: concentrated between 02:04–02:11 UTC — consistent with a brief routing disruption rather than a batch retry policy.

Proposed next steps (will execute once you confirm):
1) Prepare a split-invoice option: for any invoices with multiple line-items or multiple card tokens on file, we can create partial invoices to try alternate cards. This is manual but we can automate a one-off run for the 12 affected invoices.
2) I will open a case with the acquirer (we have a partner contact) and request the raw gateway trace — that will give us the final reason code and any network-level timeouts.
3) Provide you with an evidence bundle (AVS, last4, response_timestamps) suitable for acquirer review.

Marissa / Hannah — can you pick up the split-invoice work and estimate how long a targeted retry would take (automation vs. manual)? Also Marissa, please start the acquirer trace request — tag it Collectify-8721.

If you want immediate relief, we can also provision a one-time card-update email template to send to affected customers asking for a second card; I can share a recommended cadence.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Eli Navarro <eli@collectify.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 14:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Multiple card declines today — urgent help? (split-invoice plan + timeline)

Eli — looping in a succinct plan for your ops team. We've done this flow before with two of our mid-market customers. Action plan and ETA:

1) Inventory & mapping (1.5 hours): We’ll map each failed charge to invoice IDs and available alternate payment methods on file. (I used the CSV you shared.)
2) Create split invoices (manual override; 2–3 hours total): For invoices with multiple line items we will create a reduced invoice (50–100% of original depending on your instructions) and mark the remainder to retry later. We will flag retries with a special metadata tag so your accounting export includes the split context.
3) Targeted retries (automation script; ~2 hours to stage, then run): We will attempt retries against alternate tokens one-at-a-time with a 3DS fallback where available. Script will pause on soft declines and escalate to manual for any hard declines.
4) Evidence bundle (30–60 minutes): We’ll compile the AVS/response traces + acquirer responses into a single PDF that you can hand to your bank.

Total elapsed time from sign-off: ~6 hours. If you want us to prioritize it right now, we can be live on this within 90 minutes.

Please confirm: (A) do you want full-split (break down to single line items) or partial-split (split largest line items only)? (B) do you want us to send the card-update outreach concurrently, or only after retries fail?

Attachments: none

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Eli Navarro <eli@collectify.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 17:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Multiple card declines today — urgent help?

Marissa / Logan — appreciate the fast response and the clear plan. Confirming we want:

A) Partial-split approach: attempt to collect the largest line items first (avoids fragmenting accounting too much).
B) Start the automated retries immediately and run the card-update outreach only for those that still fail after two retry attempts.

Also, our acquiring bank sent back a preliminary note (attached) with an internal trace id: ACQ-5592 — they said they see an intermittent gateway timeout at 02:07 UTC that coincides with your reported window. They asked for the AVS + timestamped traces which you mentioned. Please include the gateway trace in the evidence bundle.

Thanks — Eli
Head of Finance
Collectify, Inc.

Attachments: acquirer_response_06010.pdf
